title: Laws Reveal What a Society Fears

voice.direction: A calm, curious guide. The hook is a genuine 'imagine'; 'Absurd?' is a light, raised eyebrow, not mockery. The origin is told quietly, almost hushed on 'and nobody mentioned'. 'A lie can be argued with. Silence can't.' is plain and certain. The lesson is clear and warm; 'Find the wound' lands softly. The CTA is friendly. No trailer voice.

lines.text: Imagine a kingdom where lying is legal, but silence is a crime.
Here, a magistrate fines a man for saying nothing.
Two hundred years ago, the city fell to a plot that everyone noticed, and nobody mentioned.
So they outlawed silence. A lie can be argued with. Silence can't.
Laws show what a people fear. Every strange law is a scar. Find the wound.
Invent one law that would make outsiders fear your kingdom.

shots.purpose: The wound behind the law: two hundred years ago the city fell to a plot everyone saw and nobody mentioned. Shown as watchers behind shutters and a street running into the dark; no violence.
shots.visual: Night street of shuttered houses; slits of light come on in window after window (everyone noticed); the street runs on into the dark. Callout at its far end: THE PLOT / Everyone saw., struck, then rust Nobody spoke.

lesson: A law shows what the society that wrote it fears, holds sacred or won't tolerate. A strange law becomes believable when it answers a specific historical problem: Velmarch outlawed silence (and left lying legal) because its city once fell to a plot that everyone noticed and nobody mentioned. Every strange law is a scar; find the wound.

music.key: C minor, resolving to C major
